title: Weird Animals
blurb: Real animal facts so strange your made-up answers might sound more believable.

prompts.text: Cats cannot taste _____, because they lack the taste receptor for it.
Octopus blood is coloured _____, thanks to a copper-based protein.
When it isn't in use, a woodpecker's extra-long tongue wraps around its _____.
When threatened, some sea cucumbers defend themselves by shooting out their own _____.
Some horned lizards fend off predators by squirting _____ from their eyes.
The narwhal's famous spiral tusk is actually a very long _____.
Butterflies taste their food using sensors on their _____.
Goats have _____ pupils, which give them a wide view for spotting predators.
Crows can remember individual human _____, and hold a grudge against them for years.
Dolphins can sleep with one _____ open, resting only half of their brain at a time.
Under its white-looking fur, a polar bear's skin is _____.
In seahorses, it is the _____ who carries the babies and gives birth.
Female Komodo dragons have laid eggs that hatched without any help from a _____.
Thanks to their great weight and stiff ankles, elephants are unable to _____.
A garden snail's ribbon-like tongue is covered in thousands of tiny _____.
Male platypuses have a venomous _____ on each hind leg.
Sharks have been around for longer than _____ have existed on Earth.
Owls cannot move their _____ in their sockets, so they turn their whole head instead.
The punch of a peacock mantis shrimp is strong enough to crack aquarium _____.
Honeybees tell the rest of the hive where to find flowers by performing a _____.
An ostrich's eye is bigger than its _____.
Hippos ooze a reddish fluid from their skin that works as a natural _____.
A tiger's stripes aren't just in its fur: its _____ is striped too.
When tickled, rats make high-pitched chirps that scientists compare to _____.
The electric eel isn't a true eel at all; it is actually a type of _____.
Crickets hear through eardrums located on their _____.
Some male penguins court a mate by presenting her with a carefully chosen _____.
A chameleon's tongue can stretch out further than the length of its own _____.
Turritopsis dohrnii, which can turn itself back into a younger form, is nicknamed the _____ jellyfish.
A flamingo's pink colour comes from its _____.
Hummingbirds can hover in mid-air and even fly _____.
Snakes pick up scents by flicking their _____.
A group of rhinos is called a _____.
A group of ferrets is called a _____.
A group of zebras is called a _____.
Sloths climb down from their trees only about once a week, mainly to _____.
A baby puffin is called a _____.
A baby echidna is called a _____.
A group of ravens is called _____.
A sloth's fur is tinted green by growing _____.
A naked mole-rat colony is run by a single breeding _____.
Dung beetles can roll their ball in a straight line at night by steering with the light of the _____.
The kakapo, the world's heaviest parrot, cannot fly and lives in _____.
A headless cockroach can survive for weeks because it breathes through body openings called _____.
Sea otters often wrap themselves in strands of _____ so they do not drift away while they sleep.
